authority.role: Pinned read-only snapshot; the Key Pattern Library remains the knowledge authority.

thesis.title: Value migration under cheap cognition
thesis.summary: As AI lowers some cognitive-execution costs, differentiated realized value may move toward selection, judgment, verification, accountability, trust, distribution, and scarce human attention.

propositions.title: Human capacity is bounded
propositions.statement: Human time, bodily capacity, and attention remain finite while generated output can expand.

propositions.title: Coordination has friction
propositions.statement: Multi-person work can introduce context loss, misalignment, compromise, politics, and drift.

propositions.title: AI reduces some execution costs
propositions.statement: AI can provide bounded cognitive execution while retaining an operator's context and objective.

propositions.title: The minimum production unit can shrink
propositions.statement: Lower context-transfer and execution costs can reduce the humans needed in a cognitive-production unit.

propositions.title: One operator can perform company-shaped work
propositions.statement: One accountable operator using agents can execute bundles of work formerly associated with multi-person organizations.

propositions.title: Lower coordination is not total effectiveness
propositions.statement: Solo-agent firms may lose independent criticism, diverse knowledge, redundancy, legitimacy, and resilience.

propositions.title: Output supply expands
propositions.statement: Inexpensive cognitive execution increases the supply of competent products, content, features, and possible actions.

propositions.title: Execution becomes less distinctive
propositions.statement: Another competent implementation differentiates less when comparable execution is broadly available.

propositions.title: Choice and verification burdens grow
propositions.statement: More possible outputs create selection, evaluation, verification, and distribution work.

propositions.title: Consequential action needs an accountable terminus
propositions.statement: Downside, liability, and oversight duties still require an accountable person or legal entity.

propositions.title: Judgment quality varies
propositions.statement: People and organizations differ in domain knowledge, taste, goal selection, and fitness recognition.

propositions.title: Trust directs scarce attention
propositions.statement: When people cannot inspect every output, reputation affects consideration and adoption.

propositions.title: Good selectors gain leverage
propositions.statement: When decisions control more downstream execution, good judgment produces more upside and poor judgment more harm.

propositions.title: Attention becomes a stronger bottleneck
propositions.statement: If supply grows faster than attention, reaching a willing audience constrains value more strongly.

propositions.title: Trust becomes a filter
propositions.statement: Trust lowers discovery and verification burdens by filtering which producers deserve attention.

propositions.title: Verification and accountability become complements
propositions.statement: More consequential machine execution raises the need to verify outcomes and preserve accountable intervention.

propositions.title: Complement demand can rise
propositions.statement: Selection, verification, accountability, trust, distribution, and attention are consumed with cognitive output.

propositions.title: Differentiated value may migrate
propositions.statement: When execution becomes cheap, differentiated realized value may move toward the scarce complements.

propositions.title: Firm boundaries remain task-dependent
propositions.statement: Compare organization designs across coordination, diversity, resilience, legitimacy, and liability.

assumptions.statement: AI capabilities remain broadly accessible rather than becoming an exclusive input.
The marginal cost of useful cognitive execution continues to decline.
Human attention does not expand proportionally with generated output.
Responsibility for consequential decisions cannot be delegated entirely to software.
Selection and verification quality remain meaningfully heterogeneous.

falsifiers.statement: AI reliably performs strategic selection better than accountable experts across consequential settings.
Large increases in output do not increase discovery, verification, or trust costs.
Trust and audience relationships cease to affect adoption, retention, or willingness to pay.
Human teams retain no measurable advantage in criticism, diversity, resilience, or error detection.
AI execution costs fail to decline or productivity stays negative across most important tasks.

attacks.challenge: Scarce or vertically controlled frontier capability may preserve execution rents.
Review, correction, and failure costs may erase measured productivity gains.
Machine filtering and delegated consumption could expand effective attention.
Insurance or certification could commoditize accountable operation.
Selection quality may converge if models outperform experts.
Complement demand can rise without differentiated value capture.
Regulation, outsourcing, taxes, or sector mix may explain solo-firm changes.

scenarios.title: Useful cognition does not get cheaper
Supply does not raise discovery costs
